question.text: REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) are typically classified as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 1.1 on page 15 of the source lists REIT units in the Dual column, and page 16 explains dual instruments as having illiquid underlying assets while the instrument itself may be liquid or redeemable. The Trap: Page 19 of the source notes that REITs, because of their listed liquidity, are also sometimes considered traditional assets — so calling them strictly "pure traditional" or "pure alternative" oversimplifies the picture. Note: The keyed answer reflects the Table 1.1 classification; the dual label captures both the listed-liquidity and the illiquid real-estate underlying.
